This application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, BNSS) seeking regular bail.
2. The applicant is the accused in Crime No.1086/2011 of Thalassery Police Station, Kannur District.

The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 498A and 306 the IPC.
3.

The prosecution case, in short, is that the applicant married deceased Nivedha on 27.03.2011 and while residing together as husband and wife in the house having Door No.TMC 31/24 which was owned by one Kiran, father's nephew of the applicant situated at Chalil in Thiruvangad amsom, the applicant subjected her to physical and mental cruelty by not allowing her to study.

Due to the continous physical and mental harassment by the applicant, Nivedha set out to Bangalore on 02.11.2011 in the evening in Kannur- Yeswanthapur train, and she committed suicide by jumping ..3..
2026:KER:26818 off that train near Temple Gate, Thalassery.
Hence, the applicant abetted her suicide and thereby committed the offences.
4. I have heard Sri.Winston K.V., the learned counsel for the applicant and Smt.V.Sreeja, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicant with the alleged crime; hence, he is entitled to bail.

On the other hand, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor submitted that the alleged incident occurred as a part of the intentional criminal acts of the applicant, and he is not entitled to bail at this stage.
The applicant was remanded to judicial custody on 25.12.2025.

A perusal of the case diary would reveal that the accusation against the applicant is very serious, and it prima ..4..
2026:KER:26818 facie shows a premeditated criminal act on his part.
The crime is of the year 2011.
The applicant was released on bail during the crime stage.
The final report was filed in the year 2013.
Thereafter, he absconded.
He was subsequently arrested in the year 2017 and released on bail.
Again he absconded and was arrested in the year 2024.

Considering the past conduct of the applicant, as rightly argued by the learned Public Prosecutor, there is every likelihood that, if he is Prashob P.P vs State Of Kerala on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35038570/
2 released on bail, he will abscond again and will not be available for trial, I am of the view that the applicant cannot be released on bail at this stage.
